item.research_question: What is the origin of the irreversible capacity loss in Li(Ni0.80Co0.15Mn0.05)O2 (NCM) cathodes during charge-discharge cycling, specifically regarding the behavior of Li ions and structural changes?
item.processing_route: Solid-state reaction: LiOH·H2O and co-precipitated hydroxide ((Ni0.80Co0.15Mn0.05)(OH)2) mixed at 1000 rpm for 15 min, then heated at 750 °C under air (20 L/min) for 8 h; electrochemical cycling in 18,650 cells at 1.0 C and 45 °C for up to 300 cycles (voltage range 2.8–4.35 V)
item.test_conditions: Cycling at 1 C rate and 45 °C for 300 cycles; APT analysis at 40 K base temperature with 25 pJ laser pulse energy; STEM imaging using CS-corrected STEM (FEI-Titan G2 and Titan Cubed)
key_findings: Capacity faded continuously to 137.5 mAh g−1 (76.0% of initial) after 300 cycles at 1 C.
Li atomic ratio decreased from 1.04 (pristine) to 0.83 after 300 cycles, while transition metal composition remained stable.
A Li concentration gradient evolved along the radial direction, with Li content increasing from the surface to the particle center.
The Li-depleted region expanded from <100 nm depth after 100 cycles to beyond ~1.5 µm after 300 cycles.
At the top surface after 300 cycles, the Li atomic fraction dropped to 0.03, compared to 1.03 in the particle center.
Structural disordering (spinel/rock-salt-like phase) at the surface was caused by TM migration from 3a to 3b sites, reducing Li accommodation capacity.
The capacity to accommodate Li ions is determined by the degree of structural disordering, with disordered structures having fewer accommodation sites.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that during cycling, transition metals (TMs) migrate from octahedral 3a TM sites to octahedral 3b Li sites in the Li layer, forming a disordered structure (spinel or rock-salt-like) that is energetically favorable. This TM migration eliminates Li accommodation sites because Li ions preferentially occupy vacant 3b Li sites but do not occupy the vacant 3a TM sites. Consequently, the disordered surface and near-surface regions have a significantly lower capacity to accommodate Li ions compared to the layered structure in the particle center, leading to a Li concentration gradient that expands with the number of cycles and causes capacity fade.
item.limitations: The authors state that STEM-HAADF cannot detect Li and O atoms due to their low atomic numbers. They also note that while local Li enrichment was observed at defects, the study does not clarify the detailed relationship between atomic defects and Li accommodation sites.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that a promising strategy for improving cycle life is to suppress the decrease in Li reservoir sites during battery operation, implying future work should focus on preventing TM migration.
quotes: The capacity to accommodate Li ions is determined by the degree of structural disordering.
The disordered structure has a lower capacity to accommodate Li ions than the layered structure.
